module_catalog.name: Academic competency in oral health 171
module_catalog.content: This module will introduce the new oral hygiene student to the dental and university environment. It will also serve as the foundation for the total oral hygiene programme and will assist the student to feel more comfortable and settled in the new environment. This module entails the following: • Professionalism and ethics • Group work and communication • Use of the library and correct referencing in assignments • Academic skills such as academic writing and reading, effective studying and how to do assignments • Dental terminology • Dental specialities • Dental instruments, equipment and materials • Dental charting • Infection control • Occupational health and safety • Basic oral hygiene care
module_catalog.contact_time: 5 lectures per week for 9 weeks, 1 practical per week for 7 weeks

module_catalog.name: Basic conversational Afrikaans 111
module_catalog.content: Basic Afrikaans grammar and pronunciation and a specific technical (oral health) vocabulary is studied and practised to enable students to converse with patients in the professional environment. In this practical module, students are required to memorise phrases and to practise conversation skills under close observation.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week

module_catalog.name: Academic information management 111
module_catalog.content: Find, evaluate, process, manage and present information resources for academic purposes using appropriate technology.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Engineering, Built Environment and Information Technology Faculty of Education Faculty of Economic and Management Sciences Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Law Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences Faculty of Theology and Religion

module_catalog.name: Academic information management 121
module_catalog.content: Apply effective search strategies in different technological environments. Demonstrate the ethical and fair use of information resources. Integrate 21st-century communications into the management of academic information.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Engineering, Built Environment and Information Technology Faculty of Education Faculty of Economic and Management Sciences Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Law Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences Faculty of Theology and Religion Faculty of Veterinary Science

module_catalog.name: Anatomy 171
module_catalog.content: The emphasis of the study in anatomy is particularly focused on all aspects of the oral cavity, but certain aspects of the anatomy of the head and neck is also included. This involves aspects of the osteology of the skull and jaw bones, the anatomy of the temporomandibular joint, salivary glands, nose, paranasal sinuses, pharynx, larynx and specific muscle groups as well as the cranial nerves, vascular supply and lymphatic drainage of the head and neck, as well as the radiographic features of some of the above.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week, 3 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Basic emergency care 171
module_catalog.content: This practical-orientated module will provide students with training in basic life support, automated external defibrillation, and first aid treatment to the suddenly ill or injured patient. The theoretical content will be offered in an interactive format where students are expected to master the content as self-directed learning. Practical skills will be demonstrated in the skills laboratory and students will get the opportunity to practice the skills under guidance and supervision.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 other contact sessions per week, 4 practicals per week

module_catalog.name: Academic English for Health Sciences 111
module_catalog.content: Proficiency in academic English by interpreting and contextualising philosophical and sociological texts prescribed during the first semester; medical ethics; study skill improvement. * Presented to students in Health Sciences only.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Academic English for Health Sciences (BNurs, BDietetics, BOH, BOT, BRad and BPhysio) 121
module_catalog.content: Academic reading as well as academic writing and presentation skills, based on the approach followed in the healthcare sciences. *Presented to students in Health Sciences only.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Microbiology and immunology 171
module_catalog.content: This module will provide the oral hygiene student with a thorough basic knowledge of: Basic microbiology Applied oral microbiology Basic immunological principles Applied immunology Principles of hypersensitivity, auto-immune disease and immunisation The module content will serve as preknowledge for clinical subjects.
module_catalog.contact_time: 3 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Oral biology 171
module_catalog.content: This module will provide the oral hygiene student with a broad fundamental knowledge on the development, normal macroscopic and microscopic structure and functions of the oral cavity, teeth and related structures. Failure or abnormalities in the developmental process leading to dental anomalies will also be covered. The module content will serve as pre-knowledge for clinical subjects and oral pathology in the oral hygiene programme.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 tutorial per week

module_catalog.name: Oral hygiene clinical practice 171
module_catalog.content: This module entails lectures and clinical work, pertaining to the scope of oral hygiene, in the pre-clinical ward. It is aimed at enabling an oral hygiene student to develop his/her skills, knowledge and attitude by means of developing, implementing and evaluating a needs-driven primary and basic-secondary preventive programme for a patient. The module will be co-taught by the Department of Odontology who will be responsible for the teaching, learning and assessment of tooth anatomy and the use of dental materials and Dental Management Sciences who will teach patient communication.
module_catalog.contact_time: 4 pre-clinical sessions per week for 17 weeks, 1 lecture per week for 24 weeks

module_catalog.name: Orthodontics 171
module_catalog.content: This module will empower the oral hygiene student to recognise and refer limited developmental and structural abnormalities of the growing and mature dento-craniofacial structures. It will furthermore provide the student with the knowledge and skills to perform orthodontic procedures pertaining to the scope of oral hygiene. This module will comprise lectures only.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 web-based periods per week for 7 weeks, 1 other contact session per week, 1 lecture per week for 19 weeks, 1 per week for 8 weeks, 1 Seminar

module_catalog.name: Physiology 171
module_catalog.content: Physiology is the study of organisms at a cellular and system level. Physiology will provide the oral hygiene student with the necessary knowledge to understand functioning and abnormalities of the human body, the vital organs necessary for normal functioning and the systems that provide essential communication for the control of the body functions and homeostasis. The module content will serve as pre-knowledge for clinical subjects.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Pharmacology 172
module_catalog.content: The aim of this module is to broaden students’ knowledge of pharmacology and relevant pharmacotherapy associated with the most common and important diseases. The learning opportunities emphasise the underlying mechanisms in which the drugs are handled by the body and how drugs affect the physiology. This will build a foundation necessary for critical evaluation of the appropriateness of pharmacotherapy, interpretation of clinical outcomes and to promote scholarly discourse.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week

module_catalog.name: Sepedi for beginners 119
module_catalog.content: *For absolute beginners only. * Students from the School of Healthcare Sciences and the School of Dentistry, who already possess the language skills taught in this module, may write an exemption examination. The acquisition of basic Sepedi communicative skills with emphasis on everyday expressions and suitable high frequency vocabulary, within specific social situations.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: isiZulu for beginners 119
module_catalog.content: *For absolute beginners only * Students from the School of Healthcare Sciences, who already possess the language skills taught in this module, may write an exemption examination. The acquisition of basic isiZulu communicative skills with emphasis on everyday expressions and suitable high frequency vocabulary, within specific situations.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Comprehensive patient management 272
module_catalog.content: The significance of the module is that trends in modern Dentistry require that the oral hygienist must possess not only exceptional clinical skills, but also exceptional relational communication between the dentist/oral hygienist and the patient, judgment and business skills to ensure a viable dental practice. This module integrates various soft-skill approaches with the clinical sciences and strives to integrate different modules in the dental curriculum horizontally and vertically in terms of clinical reasoning in order to foster professional and ethical behaviour and exceptional judgment and reasoning skills. The purpose of the CPM module is to teach students how to manage their patients and practices to ensure a viable dental practice with minimal risk. CPM interrelates with all aspects of the dental curriculum. It draws on business and behavioural and clinical research and attempts to integrate knowledge on a vertical and a horizontal plane in the dental curriculum. The critical cross-field outcomes include the following: Identifying and solving problems by using critical and creative thinking. Working effectively with others as a member of a team. Organising and managing oneself and one’s activities responsibly and effectively. Collecting, analysing, organising and critically evaluating information. Communicating effectively using visual and/or language skills in the modes of oral and/or written persuasion. Using science and technology responsibly, effectively and critically, showing responsibility towards the environment and health of others. Contributing to the full personal development of each learner and the social and economic development of society at large by making it the underlying intention of any programme of learning to make an individual aware of the importance of: Reflecting on and exploring a variety of strategies to learn more effectively; Being culturally sensitive across a range of social contexts; Developing entrepreneurial opportunities. The module comprises elements of: Comprehensive Patient Care includes application of a holistic bio-psychosocial approach towards patient care and recordkeeping in a clinical setting. The development of communication skills is a strong feature in the curriculum. Ethics and Jurisprudence includes an overview of HPCSA guidelines and regulations as well as the main laws that govern the profession. Dental Practice Management focuses on career options, leadership, strategic management, teamwork, human resource management, marketing, and general practice management
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 other contact session per week for 3 weeks, 1 seminar, 1 practical per week

module_catalog.name: Maxillo-facial and oral surgery 271
module_catalog.content: This module is designed to provide the oral hygiene student with knowledge and skills regarding: • Local anaesthetics • Oral surgery procedures • Traumatology and • Basic knowledge regarding advanced maxillo-facial surgery.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from the first year of study.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 practical per week (28 week period), 1 lecture per week for 20 weeks

module_catalog.name: Odontology 271
module_catalog.content: This module will enable the oral hygiene student to be competent in the evaluation of the oral health status of the child, adolescent, adult and geriatric patient in terms of diseases related to the hard tissues of the oral cavity plus the pulpal and peril-apical tissues, and be able to: Correctly diagnose the diseases of the hard tissues Correctly diagnose the patient’s caries risk profile Instruct a patient to be competent in self-protective measures Create resistant and optimally maintainable dental hard tissues for oral health Reverse early lesions where possible Refer patients for restorative and rehabilitative treatment Cementation of temporary crowns and the placement of tissue conditioners
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 clinicals for 30 weeks, 2 lectures per week for 16 weeks

module_catalog.name: Oral hygiene clinical practice 271
module_catalog.content: This module is a continuation of “Oral hygiene clinical practice”  in the first year of study and is aimed at enabling an oral hygiene student to develop his/her skills, knowledge and attitude by means of devising, implementing and evaluating a needs-driven primary and basic-secondary preventive programme for a patient. This module entails lectures and clinical work, pertaining to the scope of oral hygiene, on real patients.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 5 practicals per week, 1 lecture per week for 15 weeks

module_catalog.name: Orthodontics 271
module_catalog.content: This module will empower the oral hygiene student to recognise and refer limited developmental and structural abnormalities of the growing and mature dento-cranofacial structures. It will furthermore provide the student with the knowledge and skills to perform orthodontic procedures pertaining to the scope of oral hygiene. The module consists of lectures and clinical work.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week for 5 weeks, 1 per week for 8 weeks, 1 per week for 2 weeks, 1 per week for 7 weeks, 1 practical per week for 28 weeks

module_catalog.name: Periodontology 271
module_catalog.content: This module will provide the oral hygiene student with knowledge of: • Periodontal diseases • Pathogenesis of periodontal diseases • Implantology • Surgical procedures The module will also enable the oral hygiene student to: • Compile, exercise and evaluate a comprehensive and effective preventive, therapeutic and maintenance plan for the periodontal patient • Actively participate in the prevention, treatment and maintenance of periodontal conditions
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 discussion class per week for 4 weeks, 1 practical per week for 30 weeks, 2 lectures per week for 16 weeks

module_catalog.name: Public oral health 271
module_catalog.content: The module will enable the oral hygiene student to diagnose the oral health problems of any given community. Application of the knowledge gained from the module will enable him/her to participate in relevant primary and secondary preventive programmes to improve the oral health of that community in accordance with the public Oral Health Policy of the RSA. Oral hygiene students will visit special schools, nursery schools and hospitals where oral health programmes are implemented and maintained.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from the first year of study.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week for 25 weeks, 1 other contact session per week, 1 practical per week

module_catalog.name: Radiography 272
module_catalog.content: The oral hygiene student must be competent to produce a variety of intra- and extra-oral radiographs of good diagnostic quality. He/she must also recognise relevant anatomical landmarks on a radiograph and distinguish between normal and abnormal appearances. He/she must at all times be conscious of possible deleterious effects of radiation on biological systems.
module_catalog.prerequisites: All core modules from Year one.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week, 2 practicals per week (30 week period)

module_catalog.name: Counselling 371
module_catalog.content: This module will equip the oral hygiene student with the theoretical underpinning for behavioural change and the necessary skills to counsel a patient on lifestyle behavioural change. This would include, but not limited to promoting a healthy diet and smoking cessation. This would consist of both lectures and practical sessions with clients/patients.
module_catalog.prerequisites: ODO 271, OFC 271, RAD 271, PDL 271, ORD 271, GAP 271, VKM 271, TBW 271
